requirements.requirement: Reclaim duplicate payload storage within release-cache by sharing an inode only among identical files with matching ownership and mode.
requirements.summary: The two identical root-owned 0644 payload files changed from distinct inodes to one inode with link count 2. The cache pass reported one linked file and reclaimed storage.

requirements.requirement: Preserve all pathnames, bytes, ownership, and modes; keep files with different permissions independent and leave mutable files independently writable.
requirements.summary: All five files remained present with baseline SHA-256 values, ownership, modes, sizes, and mtimes. The 0600 private file and mutable/active.dat retained separate single-link inodes; mutable/active.dat remained 0644 and writable. These properties also survived restart.

requirements.requirement: Ensure a later cache pass makes no further changes.
requirements.summary: A subsequent dry run reported zero linked files and zero bytes saved, both immediately after deduplication and again after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on CentOS Stream 10 with kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 before and after the work and restart. Deduplication used the already-installed util-linux hardlink 2.40.2 utility.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct before-and-after evidence. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: node1 had pre-restart data health and a running system, acknowledged the scheduled restart, changed boot ID from d052eb57-c81d-4309-ae7f-bce362073ff9 to cf8bcf7c-3044-4d65-a6ea-5a246f32c373, and recovered to a running state with the filesystem, data, deduplication relationship, OS, and kernel intact. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: No material evidence gaps were identified. The topology has no separate application service or cluster state beyond the single node; recovery evidence therefore covers system state, mount health, and task data.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The hardlink operation was the required task mutation (cmd-2554e81d3dd143fb), and the scheduled restart was required by the provider-wide evidence protocol (cmd-a653bf699c274b33). All other commands were discovery, bounded verification, restart observation, or connection probes. The transient reboot units disappeared through reboot; no failed services, package damage, new exposure, or abandoned task files were observed afterward.
